title: Samsung Electronics applies High-NA EUV starting from 1nm
gist: At NGL 2026 in Suwon, Samsung foundry master Park Chang-min said High-NA EUV was considered for 2nm and 1.4nm but is not ready, so Samsung will only apply it in volume at the A10 (1nm) node around 2030; 0.33 NA EUV multi-patterning stays mainstream through 1.4nm and 1nm.

themes.theme: Samsung High-NA timing slips to A10

insights.claim: Samsung wanted to apply High-NA EUV to mass production at 2nm and 1.4nm but says technical improvements are still needed, pushing first volume High-NA use out to the A10 (1nm) node.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: A named-node delay of High-NA insertion pushes out ASML EXE revenue recognition timing at Samsung and lowers the near-term High-NA tool count assumption.
insights.quote: We wanted to apply High-NA EUV to mass production in 2nm and 1.4nm, but technical improvements are still needed. We anticipate that High-NA EUV will be required starting from A10 and below

insights.claim: Samsung expects to apply High-NA EUV in mass production around 2030, aligned with commercialization of its 1nm process.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Sets a concrete 2030 date for Samsung's High-NA capex wave — model ASML High-NA shipments to Samsung as a 2028-2030 event, not a 2026-2027 one.

insights.claim: Samsung's stated node cadence is 2nm already commercialized, SF1.4 in mass production in 2029, and SF1.4+ plus the 1nm process in 2030.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: A published roadmap to benchmark Samsung foundry execution against TSMC; slippage versus these dates is the cleanest signal of continued share loss.
insights.quote: Having successfully commercialized the 2nm process, Samsung Electronics plans to mass produce the 1.4nm (SF1.4) process in 2029.
insights.locator: Considering this, Samsung Electronics is expected

insights.claim: Samsung is pursuing High-NA EUV commercialization through joint development with multiple partners rather than alone, implying dependence on mask, pellicle and material suppliers to hit the A10 date.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Mask blank and pellicle suppliers gain leverage as gating items in the High-NA transition — a less-crowded way to play the node.
insights.quote: so we are proceeding with joint development with various partners

insights.claim: High-NA EUV raises the lens numerical aperture from 0.33 to 0.55, improving resolution enough to replace multi-patterning steps with single patterning at nodes that previously needed multiple exposures.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: The core economic case for High-NA is mask-layer count reduction, not raw resolution — model cost per wafer through exposure-count savings.
insights.quote: High-NA EUV is a technology that raises the numerical aperture (NA) of the lens from the conventional 0.33 to 0.55.

insights.claim: Fewer patterning steps lowers manufacturing cost and raises productivity, and single patterning also gives circuit designers greater layout flexibility.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Design-rule flexibility is an underrated second-order benefit — it can shift PPA competitiveness between foundries independent of transistor architecture.
insights.quote: Since patterning is performed only once, circuit design can also be executed with greater flexibility.

insights.claim: EUV's 13.5nm wavelength is roughly one-thirteenth that of argon fluoride lithography, which is why ArF multi-patterning can be collapsed into fewer or single EUV exposures.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Baseline physics for judging vendor claims about how far 0.33 NA EUV can be stretched before High-NA is unavoidable.
insights.quote: EUV has a wavelength that is 1/13th shorter (13.5 nanometers)

insights.claim: Samsung has applied EUV in mass production only from advanced foundry nodes of 8 nanometers and below, marking the practical entry point of EUV into its production flow.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Useful base rate for how long a new lithography generation takes to spread across a foundry's node portfolio.

themes.theme: Hybrid patterning is the base case, not High-NA replacement

insights.claim: Samsung's foundry process master expects 0.33 NA EUV multi-patterning to remain mainstream all the way through the 1.4nm and 1nm processes, with High-NA dominating only in generations after that.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Cuts against the assumption that High-NA displaces conventional EUV at 1.4nm; conventional EUV scanner demand and mask-layer counts stay elevated longer than the bull case implies.
insights.quote: Multi-patterning based on 0.33 NA EUV will be the mainstream up to the 1.4 nanometer and 1 nanometer processes

insights.claim: The industry expects EUV multi-patterning and High-NA single patterning to be used in combination in future processes rather than one replacing the other, because High-NA is technically hard and its equipment is very expensive.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: A blended-tool future supports sustained demand for both NXE and EXE platforms — bullish for total ASML units even if High-NA adoption is slow.
insights.quote: the industry anticipates that EUV multi-patterning and High-NA EUV single-patterning will be used in combination in future processes

insights.claim: High-NA adoption is gated not only by scanner readiness but by advances in related material technologies such as masks and pellicles.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Monitor EUV mask blank and pellicle roadmaps as the real gating item for the 2030 High-NA ramp.
insights.quote: Related material technologies, such as masks and pellicles, must also be advanced.
